The Purvapaksin replies [and puts forward the view that is Pūrva- paksa (F)“The transference should be of the verse itself [not of the verse set to music, as propounded in Pūrrapaksa (A)]—But it has been ex- plained that no transference of one verse into another verse is possible ‘True but there would be transference m regard to place, when it is said that Kavatisu rathantaram gäyatı”, it is true that it is not possible to sing the Rathantara over the Karali verses, hence we can take it as referring to place, the mearung being that the Rathantara is to be sung in place of the Karati verses’, the construction (the sense of the Locative) being just like what we have in such expressions as agnau tisthat’ (stays in the fire’) “kūpē tisthati’ ( stays in the well’)-Or it may be taken as referring to the details, the sense of the term ‘rathantaram being that the charac- teristic details of the Rathantara are to be extended (transferred) to the Kavati verses’,-uch details, tor instance, as ‘when the Rathantara is going to be introduced, one should think, in his mind, over Prithivi’ and so forth, this transference’ boing like what there is in a case where the Teacher having gone abroad, the pupil is told that the Teacher’s wife is your Teacher’, the meaning of which is that the service that is due to the Teacher should be rendered to the Teacher’s wife, the service being transferred to the Teachers wife " SUTRA (13). C [SIDDHANTA]-IN FACT, THE RIGHT VIEW IS THAT THE TERM SHOULD BE TAKEN AS DENOTING AN ACTION BECAUSE IN THIS THE WELL- KNOWN SIGNIFICATION OF THE WORD WOULD BE ACCEPTED AND ALSO BECAUSE THE MODIFICATORY EMBELLISH- MENT CONCERNED IS NOT DIFFERENT FROM OTHERS Bhāsya. In fact, it is not the right view that the termSaman applies to the verse and it is the transference of the verse that I meant by the text, and that we may take it as indicating either the place or the characteristic details” (as sot forth under Su 12)-Because recourse to Induect Inducation is permissible only when there is no other way. 1260 C SHABARA-BHASYA C The right view is that the term should be taken as denoting an action, 1e words like Rathantara’ should be taken as denoting the action of singing as an embellishment –Why so -The grounds for this have been already explained under Su 1 4 3, where it has been declared that The name Saman is applied to the music’, it has been seen there that the term ‘Saman’ is applied to the verse qualified by music, and there can be no conception of the qualified entity until the qualification has been conceived, hence it is this factor of qualification that is really denoted (by the word Saman’), and it is from this idea of the qualification thus obtained that there anses the idea of the qualified thing which is associated with the qualification, hence in the connotation of the term ‘Saman’, there is not the least touch of the verse (text), and on that same ground we declare that it denotes the singing (music) 4

3 Further in this the well-known signification of the word would be accepted as a matter of fact, the word gāyatı ( sings ‘) is well known as signifying the act of smging What is this act of singing”-It consists in the pronouncing of words in a particular manner,–this is what is spoken of as gāyatı sings) or ‘ganam karoti (does the singing’),-and it is this act whuch is denoted by the terms Rathantara’ and the like, as is clear from the fact that this term (Rathanlara ‘) has been used (in the text in question) along with the verb qayatı ( sings ‘), and also from the force of the Accusative ending (mathantaram’), just as in the case of such expressions as Āsāritakam gāyatı’, ’ Vardhamānam gāyatı’ We also find terms expressive of words (verbal texts) being spoken of along with the verb qayatı ‘, in such expressions as

  • Gāthām gāyalı’ (* sings C a song ‘), ‘Rcham gāyatı’ (‘sings a verse’)”

True, but the construction of the words has to be altered, what the expression means is Embellishes the verse with singing ( ganena cham samskarot’), because the ordinary construction, as it stands which would be gānēna Larot cham’ (as gayat means gānam karot ‘)-would be absurd Hence the term Rathantara should be taken as denoting the #124820 • C For the following teason also the term Rathantara’ should be taken as denoting the musi -Because the modificatory embellishment concerned is not different from others. In the case of the various Samans (Rathantar and the rest) we find that the words of the verses undergo modifications, for mstance (in the singing of the verse), short syllables become long and long ones become short, the broad’ (m accent) becomes mute ’ and the unute becomes broad and these modifications do not differ from other mochfreations which are of the nature of embellishments, for instance, by the embellishing modification of Threshing the like corn becomes the lusked me and by the embellishing modification of Pounding, the rice- grams become flow From all thus it follows that what is denoted by the words Rathantara” and the like is the embellishment in the form of singing (music) of the words (of the verse), and it is the transference of this music that meant by the text ( Kavalisu rathantaram karoti ‘) ADHYÄYA VII, PĀDA II, ADHIKARAŅA (1). C SŪTRA (14) FURTHER, THE SAMAN’ (RATHANTARA AND THE REST) IS 4 FOUND EVEN WITHOUT A SUBSTANCE Bhasya L 5 1261 4

Further, the Saman is found even without a substance,–the Same - vedins use the term substance’ (‘dravya’) in the sense of verse (Rk) hence without a substance’ means without a ter se, thus then, the meaning of the Sutra is that, as a matter of fact, the Saman is found (to be spoken of as) without a verse, for instance, there is the text-Prajapatērhrdayam- anrcham qāyat He sings the Prajupati-daya without a verse. hero we find that the particular Saman, Prajapatı-hidaya’ by name, is spoken of as appearing (being sung) without a verse -If the term ‘Sumun denoted the verse, how could the Prajapatı-hidaya (which is a Saman) be without a verse? If, on the other hand, the term ‘Suman’ stands for the musu, then, there can be music even without a veise, and in that case it becomes possible to sing the Prajāpatı-hrdaya without a verse’ -For this reason also the term ‘Saman’ should be taken as standing for the musi Says the Opponent “We have already pointed out that if the te Rathantara’ stands for the embellishment (music), then its emploviment at any time other than at the performance would be absolutely futile " In answer to this, we have the following Sulia SUTRA (15) ITS EMPLOYMENT WOULD BE FOR THE PURPOSE OF LEARNING IT FACT, IT TAKES DIFFERENT FORMS WITH DIFFERENT BASES, THE PURPOSE SERVED BY THESE IS SUPERPHYSICAL, BEING, AS IT IS A MATTER OF INSTRUCTION Bhasya IN Its employment, at a time other than that of a sacrificial performance. would be for the purpose of learning it,-1e for learning and practising it With different bases, that is, the basic things being different,-i e diverse, it takes different forms, ie the music assumes different forms with the varying bases, and hence it has got to be loaint and practised with cath individual verse (which is the basis for the Sama-music), for the purpose of acquiing efficiency and expeditiousness at the time of actual sacrificial performance it is like the case of tho Bhumirathiha (ground-charioteer) Just as the ground-charioteer draws the figure of the chariot on the ground and carries on his practice (by means of drawings) and thus exercise and practice come useful to him at the tune of the actual performance As regards the purpose served by these, Rathantara and other Samans it is super physical, it cannot be seen in the ordinary world, like the purpose that is served by Threshing and other embellishing acts -Why so 1262 SHABARA-BHĀSYA: Because it is a matter of instruction, 1.0. it is only taught as between the Teacher and his pupil–that such and such music is called ‘Rathantara’, and it is found to be nothing visible in the ordmary world Thus it is found that the objection, that it is employed at a time other than that of a sacrificial performance”, has no force at all. Another argument has been urged on the basis of the difference of names (among the various Samans, ‘Rathantara’, Brhat’, etc) -The answer to this is given in the following Sutra SUTRA (16) PARTICULAR NAMES ARE APPLIED TO IT (THE MUSIC) BY REASON OF THE DIFFERENCE IN THE MODULATIONS Bhasya C 7 Though the embellishment is one only, in the form of music there would be particular names applied to it why by reason of the difference in the modulations, though as music, it is one and the same in all cases, yet there are preculiarities, and it is on the basis of these pecu- liarities that there are different names, such as ‘Asāritaka’, ’ Vardhamānaka’ and so forth, as a matter of fact, the music known as Asārtaka’ has peculiarities which are distinct from the peculiarities of the music known Vardhamānaka’, similarly in the case cited by the Purvapaksin, the peculiarities of the music known as ‘Rathantara’ are distinct from the peculiarities of the music known as Brhat. It is on this ground that there are different names 15 SUTRA (17) C 5 THEN AGAIN, VERSES THAT FORM THE BASE (YONI’ OF THE SAMAN) AND ARE SPOKEN OF AS TO BE RECITED (SHASYA) ARE < ENJOINED EQUALLY WITH OTHERS Bhasya C י Yonishasya’ means that which is ‘yon,’ (base of a Suman) and also ‘shasyā’ (spoken of as to be recited), and what is oant is that those verses that are yoni and shasyā’ are enjoined equally with those others that are not yon and aro yet shasya’ in the following texts Fāmyāh shamsatı’ (Recites the verses sacred to Yama’), Shipuistavatim shamsati’ (‘Recites the verse containing the word ‘Shipivista ‘),–[In these two texts, two velьês ale spoken of as to be recited’, shasya, which are not the base’ of any Sāman],,- Rathantarasya yonımanushamsatı’ (Recite the verse which is the base of the Rathantara-Saman ), Brhato yonmanushamsati’ (Recitos the verse which is the base of the Bihat-Saman),-[In these two latter texts, we have two veises spoken of as to be recited, shasya’, which are also the ‘base of a Saman] In what respect are these two sets equal” “— –Thoy are equal in thus sense that both have been spoken of by means of the word 3 ADHYAYA VII, PĀDA 11, ADHIKARANA (1) C 1263 • stauti’ and shamsatı’ C

shamsatı’ (’ recites ). There are two words which, though equally expressing the act of eulogising, have yet their exact spheres strictly united; that the term stauti is applied to cases where the Mantra-teats are sung, while the term shamsati’ is applied to cases where the texts are not sung, that such is the restricted meaning of these terms is clear from the texts-(a) Pra-u-gam shamsatı’, (b) ‘Niskar- valyam shamsatı’, and (c) Āgyarh stuvatē’, (d) Prstharh stuvate’ [the Mantras mentioned in (a) and (b) are to be recited, and those mentioned in (c) and (d) are to be sung]-Thus then, inasmuch as in the text quoted above, the base of the Rathantara has been mentioned along with the verb ‘shamsatı’, it clearly shows that that base is not sung,–now it is only if the Rathantara itself were music that an unsung verse could be its ‘base’ otherwise (1 e if the Rathantara’ meant the verse, then) no verse could be spoken of as the base of Rathantara’-From all this it follows that the name * Saman’ applies to the music C , C SUTRA (18) FURTHER, THE SAMAN IS FOUND MENTIONED EVEN IN CONNECTION WITH WHAT IS NOT ITS BASE, AND IT IS ALSO FOUND C 2 MENTIONED IN CONNECTION WITH A BASE DIFFERENT IN CHARACTER FROM ITS REAL BASE”. Bhasya

(a) In the following text, the Saman is found to be mentioned in connection with a verse which is not its’ base — Sthālyām saktvavadhiyatē ityāhuryat brhad gāyatrīsu kriyatē api chainām 1ujati na cha asyām sam- bhavati’,-here we find the Brhat-Saman mentioned as being sung over a verse in the Gayatri-metre (and deprecated) -as a matter of fact, the base’ of the Brhat-Saman must be a verse in the Brhati-metre,—now if the term Saman’ stood for the verse, then there would be no possibility of the Bihat-Saman (which er-hypothesi would be the same as the verse in the Brhati-metre) to be sung over a verse in the Gayatri-metre [and hence the deprecation of it would be meaningless] -on the other hand, if the term Saman’ stands for the music, then it would be possible for the Brhat- music to be sung over the verse in the Gayatri-metre, and hence a reference to it in the text quoted,- in the words ‘yadbhrhat gāyatrīsu krvyatë”, becomes quite intelligible เ (b) Similarly, the following text shows that the Saman is used also in connection with a base which is different in character from its own ‘base ‘-’ Yo ar vichchhandası samohati sa ham samshināti sāma va vilikhati sāma samshināti icham vilikhatı’ [If one modifies the Saman to fit a wrong metre, he destroys the verse and ruins the Saman, or destroys the Saman and ruins the verse ‘],-what this means is that when a Saman is sung with a wrong metre, there must, in course of the adaptation, be some modifications made either in the music or in the words of the text; in these modifications, as between the music and the verse, that which is ‘reduced'1264 SHABARA-BHASYA: · is said to be rued’, and that which increased’ is said to be destroyed’ All this would be possible only if the term ‘Saman’ stood for the music, and not if it stood for the verse. The modifying’ also spoken of in connection with the Saman would be possible only in the music, never in the text of the verse If the term ‘Saman’ stood for the verse, then it would always have to be read as in the text of the Veda, and there could be no modification of it -For this reason also the term · Saman must be taken as standing for the music L SUTRA (19) [Objection against Su 15] WHEN THE . BASE IS ONE ONLY. THERE CANNOT BE A DIVERSITY OF FORMS -IF THIS IS URGED [then the answer is as in the next Sūtra] Bhāsya for the It has been argued (under Sa 15) that its employment purpose of learning it Agamst this the following objection is urged When the base is one only, there cannot be a diversity of forms, the Rathan- tara-music is a thing different from the Brhal-music, so that when the Rathantara-music is learnt, the Brhat-music remains unlearnt, hence it is only right that after the Rathantara-music has been learnt, the Brhat- music should be used (sung) even at a time other than that at which a performance is going on, for the purpose of being learnt -But the Rathan- tara-music by itself is a single thing, and when one has learnt its use in connection with its base, thero can be no noed for learning the same music in connection with the subsequent verses And at any time other than that of the performance, there can be no propriety in using the said music which only an embellishing facto (and can be of use only during a performance). From all thus it follows that the term ‘Saman’ does not stand for the embellishment (in the shape of music)’ The answer to this objection is given in the following Sutra SUTRA (20). IT SHOULD BE THERE ALSO, BECAUSE IT WOULD NOT HAVE BEEN ACCOM- PLISHED IN CONNECTION WITH OTHER THINGS, AS IN THE CASE COOKING’ OF Bhasya 30/ 1 3 There would be a diversity of forms in the case cited also Why -Because it would not have been accomplished in connection with other things,-1 0. in connection with other vorses as the base would be different –as in the case of cooking, just as there is a single object • Cooking’ by name, yet it assumes diverse forms in connection with diverse things, for instance, the Cooking’ of rice is of one kind, while ADHYAYA VIL, PADA II, ADHIKARANA (1) 1265 that of molasses 19 of a totally different kind, so that the man who has learnt the cooking of rice cannot know how to cook molasses, unless he learns it-Thus it is only right that even in the case cited the music should be used even at times other than that of a performance SŪTRA (21) THERE IS COMPATIBILITY ALSO OF THE WORDS Bhasya In the manner explained above, compatibility is secured among the terms denoting the Saman, and those denoting the verse, for instance. In the text “Kavatisu rathantaram gāyatı’, the term ‘Kavati’ stands for the verses, and the term ‘Rathantara’ stands for the Saman (music); other- wise (under any other view) either the term Kavati’ would have to be taken as indirectly indicating place, or the term ‘Rathaniara’ as indirectly indicating the characteristic details " From all this it follows that the term Saman’ (Rathantara etc.) stands for the music. End of Pada vi of Adhyāya VII. ADHYAYA VII. PADA III. ADHIKARANA (1): C of the , Names like Agnihotra’ are indicators transference’ of details. SŪTRA (1) IT HAS BEEN EXPLAINED THAT THE TERM IS THE NAME OF AN ACTION. WHEN I OCCURS ELSEWHERE, IT SHOULD BE TAKEN AS C INDICATING THE EXTENDED APPLICATION ACCESSORY DETAILS Bhasya OF It was declared in the beginning of the Adhyāya that we would explain later on instances of the ’transference of details by means of Names’ this is what is going to be explained now 3 C C In connection with the Kundapāyınāmayano, we read- Māsmagni- hotram juhot [‘He offers the Agnihotra for a month’], and it has been found (under 2. 3. 24) that thus Monthly-Agnihotra is distinct from the compulsory Darly Agnihotra. Now we are going to consider the presence of the term ’ Agnihotra’ in the text quoted -For what purpose has it been used here “On thus point we proceed with the statement of the Siddhanta view.-It has been explained that the term is the name of an action,—when it occurs elsewhere, it should be taken as indicating the extended application of accessory details It has been explained that the term ‘Agnihotra’ is the name of an action,-at the very outset, under Su 1 4 4, ‘There is another injunction of that accessory’,-when the said term occurs elsewhere-i e in connection with Homa offered at the Kundapäyınāmayana, it should be taken as indicating the extended application’ of details; ie the details of the Daily Agnihotra should be understood to be transferred to the Monthly Agnihotra through the name ‘Agnihotra’-Why so -The explana- tion of this is that here we have the name of one act applied to another act, and when the name of one thing is applied to another, it implies th similarity of the former to the latter, in a case where such similarity is already known, there is mere reference, as in the case of the expression Devadatta is a lion’ [where the qualities of the lion are already known to be present in the inan], but in cases where it is not already known, it is taken as enjoined (predicated), eg in the expression Make hons of this flour’ [where the making of the flour simular to the lion is enjoined]. In the case in question, the fact of the Monthly-Homa being similar to the Daily Agnihotra is not already known, and hence it is this similarity that is taken to be eujomed in the sentence ‘He offers the Agnihotra for a month’. C ADHYAYA VII, PÂDA III, ADHIKARANA (1). 1267 which means that tlus monthly offering is to be made in the same manner as the Daily Agnihotra Question The text has been construed to mean that the Monthly Agnihotra is like the Daily Agnihotra’, but] the affix ‘vatt’, denoting likeness, not being there, whence can thus notion of likeness be derived?” Answer-It is deduced from association, the term ‘Agnihotra’ is related to a sacrifice, and it can indicate the details associated with that sacrifice, such as milking of the cow and the rest, and when it can indicate these, it can also extend their application, so that even without the ‘rati’-affix (denoting likeness), the idea in question can be got at SUTRA (2) [PURVAPAKSIN’S OBJECTION TO SIDDHANTA IN REALITY, BOTH (THE AS SACRIFICES) SHOULD BE REGARDED AS INDEPENDENT BOTH ARE EQUALLY ENTITLED (TO THE NAME) Bhasya The two particles 5 and ap’ have been put in the reverse order, • the usual pluase is () ก “In reality, both these sacrifices should be rogarded as independent and the Homa of the Kunda pāymāmayana should not be regarded as preceded by (dependent upon) the Homa of the Daily Agnihotra, it i only the name that is cominon to them - Why so?”–Because both are equally entitled to the name. In the Homa of the Kundapāyınāmuyana also is entitled to the name Agnihotra’,-just as in connection with the Daily Agnihotra, there are the words Agnihotram juhot?’, so also are these same words present in the text laying down the Monthly Agnihotra (* Másam Agnihotram juhot?’), the name thus being present in connection with both sacrifices, there is no ground for making any such discrimination as that the name (Agnihotra’) applies to the Daily, and not to the Monthly, sacrifice Thus the name must be taken as common to both, and hence the name cannot be made a ground for the transference of the details (of the Daily Agnihotra, to the Monthly Agnihotra)” SÜTRA (3) [The Siddhāntin’s Reply]—BUT THE NAME IS INBORN Bhasya The relationship between tho Name and the Named is inborn so that a name should be always taken as applying to that tlung alone to which its relationship is known to be born, and not to any other thing also, because, if it did apply to both, then there would be no fixity of denotation, and hence no confidence in the gmfication of words, it has been declared already that it is not night that a word should have more than one meaning When the name ( Agnihotra) therefore cannot apply to both 36 1268 L SHABARA-BHĀSYA: sacrifices, it has to be taken as denoting the Daily Agnihotra, and as applied to the other for the purpose of asserting its likeness to that Agnihotra, thus there is no reason for taking the name as directly denoting the Monthly sacrifico Consequently the name should bo taken as indicating the transference of the details (from the Daily, to the Monthly, sacrifice, Says the Opponent” But why should you say that the name of the Daily Agnihotra has been applied to the Monthly Agnihotra, and not that the name of the Monthly Agnihotra has been applied to the Daily Agnihotra ?” In answer to this, we have the following Sutra- SUTRA (4) BY REASON OF THE PERCEPTIBLE PRESENCE OF ACCESSORY DETAILS (IN CONNECTION WITH THE DAILY SACRIFICE), THE NAME (AS APPLIED TO THE MONTHLY SACRIFICE) SHOULD BE TAKEN AS INDICATING THE PERFORMANCE OF THESE DETAILS IN THE ABSENCE OF THESE DETAILS, THE NAME WOULD NOT BE UNDERSTOOD Bhasya In the Daily Agnihotra, the presence of the accessory details is per ceptible; 1.0 wo find the accessory details laid down directly in connection with it, such as the milking of the cow is to be done in this way, the milk is to be boiled in this way, the rice is to be cooked in this way,-the fuel used at the Agnihotra should be Khadura, the oblations should be offered in this way’, and so on-From this perceptible presence of accessory details, it follows that the name really applies to the Daily Agnihotra, and when it is used in connection with the Monthly sacrifice, it must be regarded as indicating the performance of the said milking of the cou and other details, 1.0 as indicating the ’transference’ of those details-As for the Monthly Agnihotra, there are no accessory details laid down in connection with it, and in the absence of such details, the name would not be understood, I c it could not be understood why the naine Agnihotra’ had been applied to the sacrifice. Or, the Sutra may be explained as follows- -The presence of accessories is perceptible, 10 in the Daily Agnihotra. the Material and the Deity are directly laid down-’ Offers the oblation of curds’, ‘Offers the oblation of milk’, ‘Offers an oblation to Agni and to Prajapati in the evening’-From this perceptible presence of accessories, the term should be regarded as the name of a sacrifice, the name of an act,-the sonso being that the Homa offered in thus manner is named Agnihotra’ As for the other Homa (the Monthly one), its accessories are not laid down, and in the absence of such accessories, it would remain unknown, 1e it could not be known what sort of Agnihotra it was. The Month would be the form of that dqmhoba The Month cannot be a part of the action, it is a property pertaming to the 7 ADHYAYA VII, PÁDA II, ADHIKARAŅA (2). 1269 performer -Further, what the sentence in question does is to lay down the Agnihotra’ in reference to the ‘month’, and not to represent the Agnihotra by the Month From all thus it follows that Agnihotra’ is the name of the Daily Agnihotra, and the namo as applied to the other (the Monthly sacrifice) only serves to transfer the likeness of the Daily sacrifice to the Monthly one. Question"Is this then the universal rule-that whenever the name of an action is applied to another, it transfers to the latter the accessory details of the former”> Answer-That is certainly the principle hitherto arrived at. As against the said universal rule (as an exception to it) wo have the following Adhikarana ADHIKARANA (2): The name Prāyanīya’ does not indicate the transference’ of details. BUT IN THE CASE L < SUTRA (5) OF THE SATRA-SACRIFICE, THE DECLARATION SHOULD BE TAKEN AS SERVING THE PURPOSE OF * EXPRESSING A QUALITY. Bhāsya. In connection with the Garamayana wc read—’ Taishvānaro jyotistomah prāyanîyam aharbhavatı, [where the first day of the Garāmayana is called ‘Prāyaniya’],—at the Deridashiha also, the first day’ is called ’ Prāyaniya’, as declared in the text-Prāyanıoyo’tirātrah’ These two sacrifices spoken of as ‘Prāyaniya’ must be taken as distmet from one another, on the same principle of 2 3 24, as that which proved (in the last Adhikarana) tho two Agnihotras to be distinct-But in the present case, even though the name prayaniya’ has been applied to the second sacrifice, it does not indicato the transfcience’ of the details of the first, to the second, sacrifice What then is it -The declaration serves the purpose of signifying a quality-How so -It has been explained (in the foregoing Adhikurana) that it is by indirect figurativo indication that a Name indicates the trans- ference of details, but such indirect indication can be admitted only when the direct denotation of the words is not admissible,-in the present instance, however, it is only the direct denotation that is admissible, whereby the word denotes a quality; and hence by reason of the prosence of the quality in the shape of the action, the name applies to the sacrifice by direct denotation, the name ‘māyaniya’ denoting that with which they start the work’ (‘Prayantı anēna ‘),-10 that with which the performance 1270 SHABARA-BHASYA of the Satra begins. The supplementary declaration also indicates the same meaning of the name- He places the Jyotis first-the sense being that since Jyotis is Prāyaniya, therefore, Jyotis is made the first’, this is the sense of the sentence he placos the Jyotis first-From thus it follows that in the present case there is no indication of Transference’ by the Name. [The term ‘prayaniya’ denotes the first,-both the sacrifices in question are equally entitled to being called ’the first hence this case is not analogous to that of the two ‘Agnihotras’, where by leason of the presence of details in conner- tion with the Daily Agnihotra only, the Monthly Aquihotra had to be taken as entitled to the name Agmhotra only induectly Hence in the present case, the application of the name ‘Prayanīya’ to one act does not mean the transference of that act to the other act, which also is named ‘Prāyanīya | ADHIKARAṆA (3): The presence of the term ‘Sarvapṛstha’ indicates the transference’ of all the six < € Prsthas’. SUTRA (6) [PŪRVAPAKSA]— WHEN THE VISHVAJIT SACRIFICE IS SPOKEN OF AS ‘SARVAPRSTHA’, WHAT IT STANDS FOR ARE THE PRSTHAS’ CONNECTED WITH THE JYOTISTOMA. BECAUSE THE VISHVAJIT IS PRECEDED BY IT, THE TERM PRSTHA’ IS APPLICABLE (TO THEM) • Bhasya 2 There 19 the text- Vishrajit sarvapistho bhavati ‘The Vishvajit sacrifice is Sarvaprstha, 1e having all the Pistha-hymns’ | In regard to this, we proceed to consider the question-Is this a mere Reference? or an Ingunction? The Purrapaksa view on this question is as follows C CC C Tt is a mere reference-Why so It is only that which is without all the Prathas in connection with which all the Prstha’ could be enjoined, that which already has all the Pisthas’, what would be the use of enjoining the saine with regard to that As a matter of fact, the Vishrajit already has all the Prathas -How 50 *–Because the Vishwant is preceded by it,—1e because it is preceded by the Jyotistoma,-the Hymns of tho Jyotiatoma become admissible into the l’ishranit, and among them are the foun hymns, Māhendra and the rest,these are the all for thus sacrifice, wluch, by reason of these Hymns. becomes Sarvapistha (having all the Pistha-hymns’) — ‘But these hymns are not Pisthas’ The answer to that is that the term pratha 18 applicable to them 10 as a matter of fact, the term “pratha’ has been applied to the said hymns in the text “There are seventeen Pratha hymns’-Fiom all this it follows that the text in question is a mere reference " "

[What the Parapakea means 14 that (1) the foun Stotras connected with the Jyotitoma aro admissible into the Vishvant, (2) the name ‘pratha’ has been applied to those hymns,-(3) hence it is already a sacrifice with all prathas’, (+) what is already known to be adınıssible need not be enjomed,-(5) hence when the name sa vapratha is applied to the Tishvagit, it can be taken only as 1eferring to the four hymns that come into it by virtue of the general law that ’the Ectype (Vishvant) 19 to be performed like its Archetype (Jyotistoma}’] 1272 SHABARA-BHASYA: SUTRA (7) C [SIDDHANTA-THEY SHOULD COME FROM THE SADAHA’ SACRIFICE AS IT IS IN CONNECTION WITH THAT THAT THERE ARE INJUNCTIONS (OF PRSTHAS) Bhasya The text in question cannot be a reference.—What is it then It should be taken as an Injunction, a mere reference, not prompting any activity, would be useless-Then again, in connection with tho Jyotistoma, thero are not several Pisthas to which the torm ( Sarvaprstha in the text in question) could be a reference -in connection with the Sadaha sacrifice, however, there are several Prsthas, as it is in connection with that (the Sadaha sacrifice) that there are Injunctions, such as ‘From among the Pisthas, there is the Rathantara Pratha’, and so forth -For these reasons the name (Surva- pratha’, appearing in connection with the Vishvagit) should be taken as an Injunction, laying down the transferenco (of the details of the Sadaha sacrifice). 3 SUTRA (8). ALSO BECAUSE OF THE INDICATIVE TEXT Bhasya The following indicative text points to the saine conclusion- Pavamānē rathantaram karoti, ārbhavē bihat, madhye tarānı, vairūpam hotuhsāmē, vairājam maṛtrāvarunasya, razratam brahmanachchhamsinah, shahvaram- achchhāvākasya’ (1) ‘At the Pavamāna, he sings the Rathantara, (2) at the Arbhava, the Bhat, in the middle, the others, (3) the Varupa is the Saman of the Hotr-pest, (4) the Vairāja is that of the Maurūvaruna, (5) tho Raivata is that of the Brahmanächchhamsin, and (6) the Shāhvara is of tho Achchhāvāka ‘],-this text which lays down the assignment of the Sāmuns clearly indicates the Prstha-hymns pertaining to the Sadaha-sacrifico lat which, on each of the six days, they sing oach of the following Pisthas (1) Rathantara, (2) Bihat, (3) Varrupa, (4) Vairāja, (5) Shāhiara and (6) Rawata, exactly the same and in the same order as those mentioned in the text just quoted] SÚTRA (9) THE NAME ‘PRSIHA’ USED IN CONNECTION WITH THE JYOTISTOMA IS APPLIED TO THE HYMNS AFTER THEY HAVE COME INTO EXISTENCE [IE. IT IS NOT INBORN’] Bhāṣya 4 It has been argued by the Purvapaksin that the term pratha is applicable to the hymns recited at the Jyotis1ɔma’ -Our answer to this is that this 18 not " ADHYAYA VII, PĀDA TII, ADHIKARAṆA (3). ― C C 1273 name ‘prstha’ (as applied to the hymns connected with the Jyotistoma) inborn’ ie its relationship to the said hymns is not inborn, eternal], when the hymns are spoken as these Prathas’, thus name applied to them after they have come into existence [and is purely adventitious, circumstantial), this naming of them would be justifiable only if they wore aheady known by that name, but as a matter of fact, they are not known by that naine Why then are they referred to by that name (in connection with the Jyolistoma) “That is due to the presence (at the Jyotistoma) of an indicative (of that name), in the shape of the Mahendra-hymn, which also happens to be a Pistha-On the other hand, the fact of the hymns connected with the Sadaha being Pisthas is well known, because there are injunctions to that effect, as already explained (under Sú 7), consequently, it the namo prstha’ in the text in question is taken as standing for the Pisthas of the Nadaha sacrifice, the direct denotation of the term ‘pratha’ becomes accepted, while in the other cuso (if taken as standing for the hymns of the Jyotistoma), it would have to be taken in an indirect figurative sense-From all this it follows that the text indicates the transference of the P’isthas connectod with the Sadaha. C SUTRA (10) [Objection] THERE IS INJUNCTION OF TWO (ONLY) “-IF THIS IS URGED [the answer would be as in the following Sutra] Bhasya “If you view is that the text in question contains the injunction of the Prsthas connected with the Sadaha, that cannot bo right,-why?—— because the torm sarvapistha’ (if it is an Injunction) has to bo takon as consisting of two parts, it should onjoin the Prsthas, as also the fact of their being ‘all’ That may be so, what is there wrong in that?’-The wrong, we say, is that it is unpossible, if the tem prstha’ enjoms tho Prsthas, then it cannot be qualified by the term Sarva’ (all’); if the term ‘pistha’ were taken as a mere reference, then the said qualification would be possible; but the Pisthas would remam unenjoined, but while the Prathas are not there, how could their being all’ be onjoined” that both the junctions are unpossible.-What is possible however is to take the text Sarapistho bhavati’ as enjoining the ‘being all’ as relating to the Bhat and Rathantara wluch have been enjoined and are therefore admissible, the meaning of the injunction (of being all’) being that both, the Bhat as well as tho Rathantara, are to be used, and not only one. This interpretation not open to the objection pointed out above. Hence the text should be taken as onjoining these two (Bihal and Rathantara).” So1274 SHABARA-BHĀSYA: SUTRA {11} E [Answer] NOT SO; BECAUSE THE TERM SARVA’, ‘ALL’, IN THAT CASE, BECOMES MEANINGLESS Bhāṣya 30, It cannot be us explamed above-Why 7– Because the term Sana 1 all 1 ‘all’ in that case becomes meaningless, devoid of sense. The termi always stands for many things, and it cannot rightly stand for two things only-This incongruity is not there if the text is taken as laying down the Prathas connected with the Sadaha (as their number is 8C) But in that case also, the term Sarapistha’ will have two parts and the consequent incongruities (as shown above)” -Our answet to that is that it will not be it will be only the being all’ of the Pisthas that would be enjoined,— not the Pisthus themselves. It has been already pointed out that if the Pisthas are not there, m reference to what would the being all be enjoined “The answer to that is that what is enjoined by the text is the ‘being all of the Prathas, and this has got to be accomplished (in obedience to the injunction),–but it cannot be accomplished without the Prsthas -so that naturally the Prsthas also will have to come in In this manner, the term (sarvapistha’) would not have two denotations, and the use of the term ‘Sarva’, all’, would become justified. 1 C From all this we conclude that the text lays down the transference’ of the Prathas of the Sadaha C ADHIKARANA (4): The name avabhṛtha ’ indicates the ’transference’ of all details connected with the < Soma’. SUTRA (12) SIMILARLY THE AVABHRTHA’ TRANSFERS THE DETAILS ง C FROM THE SOMA’ Bhasya In connection with the l’arunapaghāsa, we read — l’ārunyü niskāsāna tusaishchāvabhi tham yant [ They proceed to the Avabhi tha with the smearings of the curdled milk and with the husks’] In regard to this, there arises the question-Does the text enjom, in regard to the Varunaprayhāsa, the Husks and the Curdled-milk-smear mga in connection with the Water-sprinkling (in all directions) which is done at the Darsha-Pūrnamāsa [and which therefore is to be done also at the Varunapiayhāsa, which is an ectype of the Darsha-Pūt namāsa] ? Or does it indicate the transference’ (to the l’armapraghāsa) of the details of the Avabhrtha connected with the Soma ? —- On this question, the Punapaksa view is as follows The text should be taken as laying down the details in reference to the Water- sprinkling connected with the Darsha-Pūrnamāsa, as this we presume to be the notion that uses from the proximity- thus connection with the details of the Darshapurnamasa being in close proximity (to the l’arunapraghāsa) by virtue of the general law (that the cetype is to be performed like the archetype’)—But this would not be drabhitha (which is what the text speaks of alabhrtham yant) The answer to this is that the term *avabhitha’ does appear in connection with the Darsha-Pūrnamāsa also, in the text’ Esa vai darshapūrnamāsa yoravabhithah This is the Aabhi tha at the Darsha-Pārnamāsa ‘|’

35

In answer to this Pūrvapaksa, we have the following Siddhänta Similarly the Arabhitha transfers the details from the Soma, 1e just as the Pisthas are transformed from the Sadaha, so In the present case the details are transfered from the drabhitha related to the Soma How so “The grounds for thus have already been explamed under Su 7 3 1. above 9 SUTRA (13) * [ObjectionТTHE DETAILS SHOULD COME FROM THE ORIGINAL ARCHETYPE (DARSHA-PURNAMASA) -IF THIS IS URGED [then the answer is as in the following Sūtra] Bhasya ‘It has been argued by us that the text in question may be taken as 1276 SHABARA-BHAŞYA an injunction of accessories in referenco to the Avabhrtha connected with the Darsha-Pūrnamāsa ;-what is the answer to that? , This Sutra is intended to be introductory to what follows in the next Sutra SUTRA (14) THAT CANNOT BE, AS (IN CONNECTION WITH THE DARSHA-PURNAMĀSA, THE MENTION OF THE AVABHRTHA) COULD BE ONLY FIGURATIVE 4 2 Bhäsya 4

What has been suggested cannot be right-Why Because there is no Avabhrtha at the Darsha-Pūrnamāsa - But we find the text Esa var darsha-pūrnamāsayo, avabhi thah”-True, there 15 thus text; but that does not unpart the character of avabhrtha’ to what has been spoken of “Why “The explanation is as follows-Of the sentence Esa ar darsha- pūrnamāsa yor avabhithah’, two interpretations are possible (1) it may be taken as laying down the connection, with Darsha-Purnamāsa, of a thing which has been recognised as having the character of Avabhitha’‚—just as when it is said that Devadatta is Yazñadatta’s son’, what is expressed is the relationship to Yagñadatta, of Devadatta who has been recognised as having the character of son -or (2) it may be taken as assorting tho character of Avabhrtha’ m a tlung which is recoguised as being connected with the Daisha-Pūrnamāsa, but is not recognised as having the character of ’ Arabhrtha’;-just as, when it is said that Tlus mango is Yapñadatta’s son’, what is asserted is the character of son’ (1e being dear) m the mango whose relationship to Yajñadatta is already recognised —Now, in the case in question, the connection of Water-sprinkling with the Dasha- Pūrṇamāsa is already known through the Context’,-what is not recognised is its having the character of Avabhitha’, henco what the text asserts is tlus character of Avabhrtha’ in the Water-sprinkling; but it does not actually become Avably tha “Thus Water-sprinkling also may be Avabhitha- [what is the harm “I”-That cannot be right, because it is not reasonable for one terin to have more than one denotation How then is the word used (in connection with the Water-sprinkling) ?"-Such use is due to simulanty (between Water-sprinkling and Arabh thu) - What similarity”–Thero is the sumilarity that both are connected with Water, on which basis the Water-sprinkling has been culogised as this is Arabhitha itsolf’, just as (in the sentence Thus mango Yajñadatta’s son’) the mango is eulogised аь зод For all these reasons, the conclusion is that in reality there is no Arablatha at the Darsha-Purnamasa, and honce the text in question cannot be taken as laying down accessory details L 1 C

SŪTRA (15) LC ALSO BECAUSE WE FIND INDICATIVE TEXTS Bhasya LE ― What The above conclusion is also supported by an indicative text is that indicativo text?"-It is thus Nāyudām juholt, na suma gayatı, ADHYAYA VII, PĀDA III, ADHIKARANA (4) 1277 na vā gamanamantram japatı’ [ He does not offor the Ayurda-oblation; ho does not sing the Saman, he does not recite the Gamanamantra ‘],- horo we have the denial of the details related to the Soma, which indicates the possible admissibility of those details-From all this it follows that the text indicates the transference of the details of the Avabhrtha connected with Soma ’ ADHIKARANA (5): The material used at the Avabhṛtha of the Varunapraghasa sacrifice should be Husks and Curdled-Milk-Smearings’. SUTRA (16). WHEN A PARTICULAR SUBSTANCE HAS BEEN ENJOINED, THAT SAME SUBSTANCE SHOULD BE USED, BECAUSE THERE IS THE DECLARA-

TION TO THAT EFFECT IF NO SUBSTANCE HAD BEEN ENJOINED, THEN ALONE COULD THE CAKE BE USED, ON THE GROUND OF ITS HAVING THE HUSKS FOR ITS ORIGINAL SOURCE Bhāṣya It has been explamed (in the foregoing Adhikarana) that the Avabhutha at the Varunapraghāsa sacrifices takes in the details of the Avabhi tha at the Soma In regard to thus, we proceed to consider the following question-At this sacrifice (Avabhrtha of Varunapraghāsa), what is the substance to bo used” Is it the Cake? 01 Husks’ and Curdled-Milk-Smearings

L
On this question, the Purvapaksa view is as follows.“It is the Cake that should be used -Why -Because the Cake comes into it through transference’ based upon the name (Arabhitha’, włuch transfers the details of the Avabhrtha of the Soma, at which latter, Cake is the substanco used) But Husks and Curdled-Milk-Smearings are the substance directly declared -True, that is the substance duectly declared; but it is not what can be regarded as enjoined, because what is enjoined is the Avabhitha– in the words Irabhitham yanti ( thoy proceed to the Avabhi thu), under the encumstances, if the saine sentence were taken as enjoming the Hushs and Curdled-Milk-Smearings,—thon there would be a syntactical spht,- (n) They proceed to the performance of the Avabhitha,—and (b) that with the substance Husks and Cudled-Mith-Smearings’ For what purpose then is the declination of the Husks and Cudled-Milk-Sincauungs-It is entirely useless, having no connection with the sacrifice at all "
9
In answer to the above we have the following Siddhanta -When a particular substance has been enjoined, that same substance should be used that is, the case in question, a particular substance has been cujomed, in the toxt-They proceed to perform the Avabhitha with Husks and Curdled-Mith-Smearings’,—hence the sacrifico should be one in wluch the substance used is Hushs and Curdled-Milk-Smearings Why so↑ " Because there is the declaration to that effect, 10–the Hushs and Curdled- Milk-Smearings is directly declared, while tho Cake could come in only through inference, by transference "

The Cake also is duectly doclared, through the name (Avabhitha’)”’ ADHYAYA VII, PADA III, ADHIKARANA (5) 1279 Even though directly declared, yet (coming in by Transforence) it comes in only in a general way, while the Husks and Curdled-Milk- Smearings coine m as specifically mentioned, and the particular always sets aside the general -Then again, the Cake is only indirectly indicated, while the Husks and Curdled-MIL-Smearings 1 directly declared, and as between Direct Declaration and Indirect Indication, the acceptance of the former more reasonable Hence at the sacrifice in question, the sub. stance used must be the Husks and Curled-Milk -Smearings

It has been argued (by the Purvapaks) that the Husks and Curdled- Milk-Smearings cannot be connected with the Anubhitha, becauso, if it were, then there would be syntactical split” -Our answer to that is as follows If tho Husks and Curdled-Milk-Smearings were enjoined apart from the Avabhatha, then there would be syntactical split, what however is actually enjoined is that new type of Avabhitha at which the substance used Is the Husks and Curdled-Milk-Smearings, so that there is nothing in- congruous in the injunction of an act (sacrifice) along with a particular accessory detail If, on the other hand the Husks and Curdled-M ¿th- Smearings were not enjomed, then its mention in the text would be entirely meaningless-Hence we conclude that at the sacrifice in question the substance used must be the Husks and Curdled-Milk-Smearings. If no substance had been enjoined, then alone could the Cake be used. on the ground of its having the Husks’ for its original source, 10 if no particular substance had been directly laid down, then alone could the Cake be used, by reason of its having the husks for its source, as a matter of fact, however, a particular substance (Husks, elc) has been directly laid down, hence the Cake cannot be used ADHIKARANA (6): The term ‘vaisnava’ does not indicate the ’transference’ of the details of the Atithya. Bhasya (A) In connection with the tithya, we read- Vaisnavo navakapālo bhavati’, [The Cake baked upon nine pans is to be dedicated to Visnu ‘1,- (B) and in connection with the Rajasuya, we read—’ Pūrvasmın tiisamyuktē vaisnavasti ikapālah’ | At the previous Tisamyukta, the Cake baked on three pans is dedicated to Visnu ‘] · The question to be considered is this-In the sentence At the Trisam. yukta, the Cake baked on three pans is dedicated to Visnu-dors, or doos not the term dedicated to Visnu’ mean the transference’ of the details of the Atithya (in connection with which also, the same torm, dedicated to Visnu’ has been used)? The Purvapaksa view is as follows “The term does mean the trans- ference of these details -Why Whenever a term has boon used in connection with a sacrifice of which the details have been prescribed,—if that same term is found used in connection with another sacrifice, whose details have not been prescribed, then the indication of that term is that the details of the former are to be transferred to the lattor sacrifice, this is what has been made clear under 7. 3 1. In the present case, we find that the term dedicated to Visnu’ has been used in connection with the Atuthya, the details of which have been prescribed, and it is found to bo used (in B) in connection with the Trisamyukta sacrifice, of which the dotails are not prescribed, hence it follows that the term indicates the transference to this latter, of the details of the former " In answer to this, we have the following Siddhanta SUTRA (17).

IN REALITY, IT IS ONLY THE INJUNCTION OF AN ACCESSORY, IT COULD
NOT INCLUDE THE DETAILS, BECAUSE IT IS EQUALLY
PRESENT (IN BOTH)
Bhasya
The term in question should be taken as enjoining an accessory, what it enjoins 18 an accessory of the Atthya sacrifice, in the shape of the connection of Visnu as the deity, hence it cannot include within itself the details of that sacrifice” Why so “-Because it is equally present in both, ie the terin is equally there. in connection with the Atthya and the Trisamyukta, just as it enjoins the deity Visnu at the Atthya, so it does also at the Tsamyukta,—and it is only if this direct denotation of the torm were found to be inapplicable that there could be a justification for taking the term as indirectly indicating tho transference of the details (of the Anthya),- -in the prosent case however the direct denotation of the term-viz the injunction of the deity Visnu,— -is found to be quite com patible; hence it cannot be taken as indicating the said dotails
ADILIKARANA (7): Words like ‘Nirmanthya’ are not indicative of the ’transference’ of details.
SUTRA (18)
THE SAME IS THE CASE WITH TERMS LIKE NIRMANTHYA’.
Bhasya
(A) In connection with the Aqnisomiya Animal, the Nirmanthya Fire has been laid down.-(B) Agam, there is a text in connection with the Agni- sacrifice, begining with the words Sādhyā var dēvāh’, and ending with * Numanthyēnēstakāh pachants’ ‘They bake the bricks on the Nirmanthya Fue-The term ‘Nirmanthya Fire’ means ‘Fire produced by the rubbing together of two sticks’ There are two things connected withi the Darsha-Purnamāsa―(1) the Grass, and (2) the Clarified Butter, and both of these are spoken of also m connection with the Pashu sacrifice,-and with certam details (1) the frass, m regard to which there is the detail ‘(‘overs the Post-hole with hass’, and (2) the Clarified Butter, in regard to which there is the detail Anomts the Post with Clarified Butter’

Now in regard to this, there arises the question-Do the words like Numanthya’ mclude (m then denotation) the related details, or not?
In answer to this question, the conclusion arrived at in the foregoing Adhikarana is extended m its application to the present instance –The same is the case with terms like Numanthya’, that is, just as it has been found to be in the case of the terin Vaisnava’, for here also the term “Nirmunthya’ is taken in its etymological sense, denoting the Fire produced at the time of the action by the rubbing together’ ( manthana’) of two sticks - Similarly the terms ‘vathis’ (Grass) and agya’ (Claufied Butter’) aro denotative of substances –So that all these three have their purposes fulfilled by signifying their direct denotations, and as such cannot include (extend their denotation to) the details Honce we conclude that terins liko those do not include the details in their denotation

ADHIKARAṆA (8): The words ‘dvayoh pranayanti”, ‘fetch the Fire at the Two’, do not indicate the ’transference’ of the details relating to : Soma ‘.
•
Bhasya
In connection with the Chaturmasya sacrifice [of which there are four parts (1) Taishvadēta, (2) Varunapraghāsa, (3) Sākamëdha and (4) Suna- siriya], we read Drayoh pranayanti, tasmāt dvābhyamēt The fetch the Fire at the two, hence they go up with two | This Fetching of Fue is found to be laid down with certain details, in connection with the Soma- sacrifice while in connection with the Darsha-Purnamasa, it is found to be laid down without any details

In regard to this, there arises the question-Is the Fetching of Fire’ spoken of m connection with the Chaturmäsya meant to be that connected with the Soma-sacrifice (with its details) Or that connected with the Darsha-Purnamāsa ? 7 On this question, we have the following Purrapaksa set forth m the Sutra itself ― SUTRA (19) [PURVAPAKSA THE FETCHING OF FIRE MEANT SHOULD BE TAKEN TO BE THAT CONNECTED WITH THE SOMA-SACRIFICE BECAUSE THE OTHER NEED NOT HAVE BEEN MENTIONED AT ALL’ LE Bhasya The Fetching of Fire’ meant should be taken to be that connected with the Soma-sacrifice Why so ‘Because the other,e that connected with the Darsha-Purnamasa-need not have been mentioned at all, as its admission into the Chaturmasya would be secured by the general law (that the Ectype is to be perforined like the Archetype’, the Darsha-Pūrna- māsa being the Archetype of the Chūturmāsya) But how can the ten Fetching Fire, which denotes merely the Felching of Fue un general, signify the particular Fetching of Fire (related to the Soma-sacrifice) ‘–It is through indirect indication, we toply, like the term intha’, just as the term tu tha’ denotes only a fort, a descent into a vc, yet, sometimes it is taken in the sense of a particular ford or descent into a river, which is peculiarly sacred and conducive to merit, eg m the expression thayātrām yaṭaḥ’ ¿ gone on pilgrimage to a sacred place ). ADHYAYA VII, PĀDA III, ADHIKARAṆA (8). SUTRA (20). [PURVAPAKSA concluded]” THE PROHIBITION OF THE VEDI’ ALSO POINTS TO THE SAME CONCLUSION Bhāsya "” 1283 C UTTARA- “There is the prohibition contained in the text-They do not go to the Uttaravēde at the Varshvadeva, nor at the Sunāsiriya’, this prohibition would have a sense only if what is prohibited were possible [so that this indicates the possibility of the Uttaravědi in connection with the ‘Fetching of Fire’ at the Chūturmāsya], and the Uttaravedi can be there only in connection with the Fetclung of Fire’ at the Soma-sacrifice, there being no Uttaraved at the Darsha-Purnamāsa " [SIDDHANTA

SUTRA (21). C IN REALITY, THE FETCHING OF FIRE’ MUST BE TAKEN TO BE THAT RELATED TO THE ARCHETYPE, BECAUSE " IT IS NOT A PROPER NAME C Bhasya 5 The Fetching of Fire spoken of here must be taken to be that related to the Archetype-e. to the Darsha-Purnamasa Why so “Because it 18 not a proper name te the term Fetching of Fire’ is not the proper name of the Fetching’ related to the Soma-sacrifice, that is to say, the term 19 not specifically expressive of that Fetching of Fe, if the term were speci- fically expressive of that Fue-fetchung, then it could denote the same in the case in question also, as a matter of fact, however, the term is the generic name of what is signified by its component parts (Pra+nayana), that is, it oxpresses the fetching (nayana) forward (prāk), so that all that it can signify is the fetching forward of the Fire, hence it must be taken as signifying that, and as tlus is present in the Darsha-pūrnamāsa, which is in close proximity (to the Chāturmāsya), by accepting the said signification, the notion of thus latter does not becomo set aside f F As regards the argument that it would be as in the case of the term tir tha our answer is as follows -The term ’tha also really denotes only ford (or descent into river) in general, as for the expression tirtha- yātrām gatah’, it is used generally after certain particular fords have been spoken of, and it is on thus account that the torm is understood as refering to a particular place of pilgrimage In a case where the term is used by itself (without reference to any particular places), it denotes only Ford in general, as for instance. Tithe snati tīrthamēra samānānām bhavati’ [ Bathes at a ford, and thereby becomes like a ford among hus equals - Then again, so long as a term can be taken in its directly denoted sense, there can be no justification for accepting an indirectly indicated one, and in the presont case, the directly denoted sense (Fetching in general) is quite compatible, 371284 SHABARA-BHĀṢYA: hence the indirect indication (of the particular Fetching connected with the Soma-sacrifice) should not be accepted. SUTRA (22). THE MENTION (OF FETCHING RELATED TO THE DARSHA-PURNAMĀSA) MAY BE TAKEN TO BE (a) FOR THE PURPOSE OF PRECLUSION, OR (b) FOR THE PURPOSE OF INDICATING AN ACCESSORY, OR (c) FOR THE PURPOSE OF COMMENDATION. Bhāsya. Says the Opponent-“It has been argued above that the other need not have been mentioned at all’ (Sū. 19), what is the answer to that "” The answer is as follows -The mention may be taken to be (a) for the purpose of preclusion-the sense being that thev fetch the Fire at the two- not at the four, or (b) for the purpose of indicating an accessory; or (c) for the purpose of commendation, continued in the expression ‘Hence they go up with two ‘.-Now (a) in every case of Preclusion, there are three objections ;-(6) as for an accessory, there is none mentioned at all,—(c) hence the only alternative left is that it is for the purpose of commendation “But Commendation also would be futile, as the Fetching is already admissible through the injunction itself “The purpose served by the commendation we shall explain under the following Adhikarana, under Sū 21 ADHIKARANA (9): The words Fetch the Fire to two means the Fetching of it at the two middle parts of the Chaturmasya. SUTRA (23)

[PURVAPAKSA” THE ‘FETCHING OF FIRE’ SHOULD BE DONE AT THE FIRST AND LAST PARTS, BECAUSE OF THE PROHIBITION RELATING E TO THE 4 UTTARAVEDI Bhāsya. 3 33 There is the text They fetch Fire at the two parts’. In regard to this there arises the question-at which two parts shall the Fetclung be done? The apparent view being that there is no restriction, the Pūrvapaksa View is as follows “The Fetching of Fire should be at the First and Last Parts-why-because of the prohibition relating to the Uttaraved, the Uttaravēdi is prohibited in the text-At the Taishvadeva thev do not go to the Uttaravědi, nor to the Sunasiriya’ [Taishraděru and Sunāsiriya are the first and last parts of the Chaturmasya] What is meant by this Fetching of Fire’ is the placing of Fire on the Uttararēdi, hence whenever there is the Fetching of Fire’, there should be the Uttaravēda; and there can be prohibition only in regard to such place and time at which the thing prohibited is likely to be, and as a matter of fact, the Uttaraved is there only at the First and Last parts of the Chatur masya, hence the ‘Fetching of Fire should be done at these two parts " * C SUTRA (24) [SIDDHANTA IN REALITY, IT SHOULD BE AT THE TWO MIDDLE PARTS, ON ACCOUNT OF THE COMMENDATORY DECLARATION REGARDING ‘GOING’ Bhasya. The ‘Fetching of Fire’ should be done at the two middle parts,-why -because of the commendatory declaration regarding going’, the fetching of Fire at the two middle parts is spoken of in the commendatory declaration Therefore they go up with two’ These two parts are described as ’two thighs’ in the text-These two, the larunapraghāsa and the Saku- mēdha, are the two thighs of the sacrifice’thighs are the limbs whereby going (locomotion) is accomplished, hence the sense of the commendation comes to be thus-There are two thighs of the sacrifice-the Varunapra- ghāsa and the Sākamëdha,-hence they fetch the fire at these two, hence it is 1286 SHABARA-BHĀSYA: that the sacrifice is accomplished by means of these two thighs,—by the fetching of Fire they become strengthened, on account of the multiplicating of details at the Fotclung-rite’ -This is the purpose served by the commendatory declaration As regards the argument based upon the ‘prolubition of the Uttaravēdi’, -our answer is as follows- C SUTRA (25). THE PROHIBITION REGARDING THE UTTARAVEDI IS IN REFERENCE TO AN ISOLATED DECLARATION THEREOF. Bhasya In connection with the Chatur māsya sacrifice, the Uttaravēdi has been spoken of without reference to any particular part of that sacrifice, m the text- Upātra vapanti’ [They place the Fire on tlus’], and it is of this Isolated declaration that there is the prohibition put forward by the Purvapaksin [ They do not go to the Uttaraved, at the l’aishradēra ‘] — “But as a matter of fact, the text ‘Upātra vapantı’ occurs at the end of the sentence declaring the accessories of the Varunapraghāsa, and hence the atra’ (‘at this’) must refer to the Varunapraghasa [so that the declaration of the Uttaraved is not isolated, it is connected with the Varuna piaghāsa]” -That cannot be, though ‘Context’, the said declaration should pertain to the Chūturmasya itself (not to any particular part of it), if the declaration of the Uttaraved had pertamed to the Varunapiaghāsa in particular, then all the other three parts would have been mentioned in the prolubitive text (which however mentions the Vaishradera only)” The declaration of the Uttararēdi might pertam to the two parts (the Varunapraghāsa and the Sākamēdha) “-Our answer to that is that the content does not belong to anv tuo parts, it belongs either to the Chāturmusya as a whole or to the Varunapraghāsa, if the context belonged to the Varunapaghāsa. then there could not be the mention of tuo parts in the prohibition, hence the declaration (regarding the Uttararēdi) must be regarded as pertaming to the Chātu māsya sacrifices as a whole “Even with all thus, we have learnt from the commendatory declaration that the Fetching of Fue should be done at the two middle parts of the Châturmāsya, why, then, should the Fetching of Fire’, thus known already (through the commendation) as to be done, be mentioned again ?” The purpose of this has not been mentioned, and no other purpose being there, we might regard Preclusion as the purpose served by it. But objections against Preclusion have been set forth before. Hence the second mention of the Fetching of Fire should be taken as being for the purpose of laying down accessories “But there is no accessory here “The accessory is mentioned in the shape of the placing of Fire on the Uttaravēdi, hence the second Fetching of Fire must be taken as being for the purpose of the said placing of Fire’ on the Uttaravedi ADHYAYA VII, PĀDA III, ADHIKARAṆA (9). 1287 [Kumaila does not accept the above presentation of the last two Adhikaranas 8 and 9 According to him, all these seven Sutias, from 19 to 25, constitute a single Adhikarana, where thire views are set forth (1) that the ‘Pranayana ’ meant for the Châāturmāsya should be that connected with the Archetype, Darsha- Purnamasa-this is the first Purvapaksa,—(2) that it should be that connected with the Soma-sacrifice, this is the second Purvapaksa, and (3) that it is an entirely independent Pranayana for the Chaturmasya only,-this is the Siddhanta, and the further conclusion is that this independent Pranayana 18 to be done at the two middle parts-See Tuptikā, pp. 159-160, also Bhattadipika, Vol II, p. 22] C ADHIKARANA (10): Such words as Svarasama’ and the like are indicative of the of details. SUTRA (26). C transference’ THE TERMS ‘SVARA-SAMAN’, ‘EKAKAPALA’ AND ‘AMIKṢA’ ALSO [ARE TO BE TAKEN AS INDICATIVE OF THE TRANSFERENCE OF THE DETAILS], BECAUSE WE FIND INDICATIVE TEXTS Bhāsya C (A) (a) In connection with the Gavamayana sacrifice, we read- Abhito divākirtyam ahastrayah svarasāmāno bhavanti’ [‘At each of the two ends of the Dwākirtya Day-1.e the one day at the centre, between the two ‘Half-year-periods there are three days called Svara-sāman ‘], in connec- tion with these Svarasāma-days (1e the sacrifices performed on those days), certain details have been laid down, such as they are seventeen’, ’they are taken up by the continuous Atigrāhyā’, and so forth (b) Then elsewhere we read-Pisthyah sadahah dvau svarasāmānau’ [‘There are six days related to the Prathas, there are two Siarasama-days ‘]—(B)-(a) In con- nection with the l’aishradera (at the Agrayana sacrifice), we read- ‘Dyaιāpithiya kakapalah’ [ The Cake baked on one pan, dedicated to Dyaus-Prthivi ‘], and in relation to this Bhakapula Cake. there are certain details laid down-Offers the Sarvahuta oblation’, ‘Makes the offering, without turning back’-(b) Again elsewhere we read-’ Kāya ēkakapālah [‘The Cake baked upon one pan, dedicated to Ka’](C) (a) Again in connection with the Vaishvadeva, we read-Varshvadēvyāmıksā’ [‘The Curdled-Milk dedicated to the Vishvēdēvas’]; and in connection with this Curdled-Milk, certain details have been laid down (b) Again elsewhere we read ‘Maitrāvarunī āmiksā [‘The Curdled-Milk dedicated to Mitra- Varuna’].

In regard to all this, there arises the question (A) Does,- ‚—or does not,- the term Svarasāman’ occurring in the second sentence (A) (b) indicate the transference of the details of the Srarasāma days connected with the Gavamayana [mentioned in sentence (A) (a)]-Similarly (B) does,-or does not the term Ēkakapāla’ occurring in the sentence (B) (b) indicate the transference of the details of the Ekakapala mentioned in (B) (a) ?— Lastly (C) Does, or does not, the term ‘Amiksa’ as occurring in the sentence (C) (b) indicate the transference of the details of the Amiksa mentioned in (C) (a)? On this question, the Purvapaksa view is that-“Every one of the three sentences in question is the injunction of an accessory, and it could not include the details, because it is equally present in both (Sū. 7. 3. 17): hence the terms in question do not indicate the transference of the details ADHYAYA VII, PĀDA III, ADHIKARAṆA (10). 1289 In answer to this, there is the following Siddhānta -The terms ‘Svara- sāman’, ‘āmiksa’ and ‘ēkakapala’ are to be taken as indicating the trans- ference of the details-Why so -Because we find indicative texts; wo find such an indicative text as leads us to conclude that every one of the terms in question is indicative of the transference of details. L E (A) As regards the term Svarasāman’,-after having declared that There are six days connected with the Prathas, and two are Svarasama- days’, the text goes on to say-Tatra yat trtiyam saptadashamahah tat trayastrimshasya sthānam abhiparyäharanti, sa uttarānām stomānāmaıyavā- yāya; tryānām cha saptadashānām anūchīnatāyāh’.-Now if these two Svarasama days (the seventh and eighth days of the Sadaha) also take in the details of the Gavamayana, then they also would have the seventeenth hymn; and in this way we get the seventeenth hymn thrice, on three consecutive days (one, the last day of the Sadaha and the seventh and eighth days, the Starasāma days, following that day), and thus we get the continuity spoken of in the commendatory words ‘Trayānām saptadushānām anüchīnatāyar’ [At the Sadaha sacrifice, on the six days the use of the following six hymns respectively becomes possible under the general law (iclating to the Archetype and the Ectype) (1) Trurt (3), (2) Panchadasha [15], (3) Saptadasha [17], (4) Ekavimsha [21], (5) Trinava [27] and (6) Trayastrimsha [33],-but what the text quoted lays down is that on the sixth day, the seventeenth hymn should be used instead of the thirty-thard, and m commendation of this thore are the words Trayānām, etc And on the Svarasama days, there is the seventeenth hymn What is secured by this is that we have the seventeenth hymn on the sixth day of the Sadaha, and on the two following days (the seventh and the eighth) which are Svarasāma days, and as such take in the seventeenth hymn This 18 the Continuity which is one of the details laid down in connection with the Gavā- mayana ]

C C (B) Similarly in connection with the Agrayana sacrifice, having laid down the Cake baked on one pan, dodicated to Dyaus-Pithivi’, the text goes on to say-Yat samahutam karoti sā tu ēkā parichaksā, huto hutah paryāvartatē sā dvitiyā, āzyasyava dyārapithevyau yajeta’,-here the sentence enjoins the use of Agya (Clarified Butter) [in place of the ‘Ekaka- pala’, Cake baked on one pan], and in connection with this sanie, this sentence indicates the presence of the two features of Sarvahoma’ and Aparyavrite’, which are the details connected with the Vaishvadēva, [at the second offering of Ekakapala] C (C) Lastly, in connection with the Curdled-Milk dedicated to Mitra- Varuna’, we read-‘They do not deal with the whey, this prohibits the offering of whey, which is a dotail related to the Vishvēdēvas, and thereby indicates the possibility of such details finding place therein. From these indicative texts we learn that cach of the three terms in question (‘Svarasāman’, ‘Ekakapāla’ and ‘Amiksa’) is indicative of the transference of details 4 C What has been said above regarding the offering of whey’ 18 on the understanding that the said offering is an act of disposal and hence stands on the same footing as the Svrstakrt offering’. C 1290 SHABARA-BHĀSYA. Says the Opponent “You have cited indicative texts, how do you establish the fact of the details actually finding place in the respective sacrifices ? “1 Answer The admission of the details is got at by Indirect Indication, and Indirect Indication is accepted on the basis of the said indicative texts SUTRA (27) OB, IT MAY BE DUE TO THE INJUNCTION (OF CHARACTER) BEING COMMON Bhasya (A) The character of Svarasāman’ is common (to the Gavamayana and the Sadaha), (B) The character of ‘Ekakapala’ is common (to the offering to Dyaus-Prrthivi and the offering to Ka); and (C) the character of Amiksā’ is common (to the whey offered to Vishvēdēva and that offered to Mitra- Varuna), and the admissibility of the details would be determined according to the principle explained below under the Sutra Yasya lingamartha- samyogat’ (8. 1. 2). C ADHIKARAŊA (11): In such expressions as Vaso dadāti’, 4 gives the cloth’, the term ‘vāsas’, ‘Cloth’ stands for the genus. Bhasya. Somewhere in the Veda, it is said- Vaso dadāts’ (‘gives away cloth ), ‘Ano dadātr’ (gives away the cart ‘) What is to be considered in this connection is-does-or does not, the use of the word ‘vāsas’ (Cloth), or ‘anas’ (cart) indicate the act (of weaving which is involved in the making of the Cloth, or of wood-cutting and the rest involved in the making of the Cart) -In this connection it has been said that what has really got to be considered 19-are these two words used m the sense of the actions (involved in the making of the two things) Or in that of the two genuses (Cloth’ and Cart ‘) If they are used in the sense of the actions, then their presence in the sentences would mean that the actions (the actual operations) have to be performed at the time of the giving, if. on the other hand, they are used in the sense of the genuses, then it does not mean this " “The two words The Purvapaksa view on tlus question is as follows are to be taken as used in the sense of the operations (of weaving and wood- cutting, etc)—Why so -Because they are found to be applicable only when the operations have been there, that is to say, the two words are applied to that substance-Yams, or wood-over which the weaver or the carpenter has performed the operation (of wearing or wood-cutting, etc), they are never applied before the said operation has been performed, hence it follows that the words are used as standing for those operations-It is on the basis of this notion of the words standing for the operations that we have the following- SUTRA (28). ‘[PŪRVAPAKSA]—” WHEN THE PRODUCT OF AN OPERATION IS SPOKEN OF, WHAT IS INDICATED AS TO BE DONE IS THAT OPERATION, AS IS C FOUND IN THE CASE OF THE YOPA’ (‘SACRIFICIAL POST’) Bhāsya. “When a thing like Cloth, which is the product of an operation, 18 spoken of, what is indicated as to be done is that operation -How sods us found in the case of the Yupa, the term ‘yupa’ is applied on the basis of such operations as cutting and the rest, and whenever it is used, it indicates the performance of all those operations, so also in the case in question’ 1292 SHABARA-BHĀŞYA: SUTRA (29) [SIDDHANTA IT IS THE MATERIALISED THING (THAT SHOULD BE GIVEN) BECAUSE THE OPERATION DOES NOT FORM PART (OF THE DENOTATION OF THE TERM) Bhasya 4 The answer to the above is as follows -The two terms are not used on the basis of the operations -Why -Those terms whose use is based upon certain definite conditions are used only when those conditions are present, eg terms like Dandin’ (Man with the stick ‘), Chhatrın’ (“Man with the umbrella’) The words in question however are found to be used when the operations are not present, being used in reference to the genus only C The following argument is urged here- What really happens is that the speaker uses the term after having inferred the operation from the genus denoted by the term [so that the word is really used on the basis of the operation]” Our answer to this is as follows-There can be no reason for abandoning the perceptible basis (in the shape of the genus) of the use of the term, and assuming its basis in the operation which is not perceptible It has been argued that- The term is used only after the operations (that have brought into existence the thing denoted by the term) “—Our answer to this is that prior to the operation, the genus was (there, but) un- manifested; and it becomes manifested by means of the operation, it is for this reason that the term is used after the operation From all thus it follows that the terms in question should be taken as used on the basis of the genuses (denoted by them). C Such being the case, what is to be done (in accordance with the injunction gives away cloth’, or gives away the cart’) is that the materialised thing should be given [and not that the operation of weaving, etc. should be performed] “Why so " -Because the operation does not form part of the denotation of the term, as a matter of fact, the operation does not enter into the denotation at all, as there is no term denoting the operation-As regards the Yupa (Sacrificial Post), in connection with that Cutting and the other operations have been directly laid down by the texts [which is not the case with such ordinary things as the Cloth and the Cart], hence the analogy is not correct. C ADHIKARAṆA (12): At the Gargatriratra’, the ‘Kindling” is done of the ordinary unconsecrated Fire. SUTRA (30) WHEN THERE IS A DOUBT, IT SHOULD BE THE ORDINARY FIRE, AS THAT SERVES ALL PURPOSES. Bhasya At the Gargatru ātra, they sing the Ajyadoha Samans:-in connection with these we read-Agnimupanidhaya stuvate’ [‘They sing the hymns after having kindled the Fire’] In regard to thus, there arises the question-Is this Fire that is kindled, the ordinary unconsecrated fire or the Vedic Fue (Fre consecrated with Vedic rites) ? On this question, the Purvapaksa view is as follows “It should be the consecrated Vedic Fue-Why Because that Fire has been brought into existence for the performance of all rites, the words used by the consecrator being Whatever rites I shall perform, and whatever rites I am entitled to perform, etc Hence in the case in question, it is the Vedic Fure that should be kindled " 3 In answer to this, we have the following Siddhanta When there is a doubt, it should be the ordinary Fire, as that serves all purposes. That is, whenever there is a doubt as to whether the ordinary or the Vedic Fire should be used, it is the ordinary one that should be used It has been argued by the Purvapaksin that the Vedic Fire has been brought into existence for the performance of all rites, and hence it is the Vedic Fire that should be kindled " -Our answor to this is as follows SUTRA (31) IT CANNOT BE THE VEDIC FIRE, AS ITS PURPOSE HAS BEEN EXPRESSLY DEFINED Bhasya The Fire meant in the present connection cannot be the Vedic one-that 18, that Fire which has been brought into existence according to the method prescribed in the scriptures, because the purpose of such a Fire has been expressly defined by the scripture itself,-’ He pours oblations into the Ahavaniya Fire [It is the Vedic Fire that is called ‘āhavaniya ‘], and so on. If the Vedic Fire were taken as serving the purpose of all rites, then the express declaration of its purpose would be meaningless. Hence it is the ordinary Fire that should be kindled In the case of the ordinary Fire, it could be regarded as serving all purposes, in the sense that it is kindled1294 SHABARA-BHASYA: in connection with each act that is to be performed with it, so that in the case of the ordinary Fue, there is no inconsistency in its serving all purposes and yet having its purposes expressly defined. Question “Why cannot tho Dhaiona Fires (1 e the Fires that have been taken to the seats of the Agnidhia and other priests) be kindled for the purpose in question [1e in connection with the singing of the Ayadoha- Samans at the Gargatrırātra] " The answer to thus is given in the following Sutra SUTRA (32)

THE COMING INTO EXISTENCE OF THESE OTHER FIRES ALSO WOULD BE LIKE THE SAME, THEY BEING SIMILAR (TO OTHERS) Bhasya Of these other Fires,- - e. of the Fires that have been taken to the scats of the priests-the coming into existence is like the same,-1 e (like the Vedic Fire), these also cannot serve the purpose of all rites-Why so *-Because they are similar; 1e these Fires are similar to the other Fires, ie the purpose of these also has been expressly defined,-in such texts as, ‘Seated to the east, he pours Clarified Butter on to the Fires that have been taken to the Priests’ seats’-From this it follows that these also are not the Fires that have to be kindled in the case in question 0 ADHIKARANA (13): The term ‘yupa’ used in the sentence C Upashayo yupo bhavati’ does not indicate the performance of the consecratory rites in connection with the Upashaya. SUTRA (33) [PURVAPAKSA]” IT SHOULD BE CONSECRATED; BECAUSE THE TERM CONNOTES CONSECRATION Bhasya "” In connection with the Ekadashini (the group of eleven Sacrificial Posts), we read The Upashaya is a Sacrificial Post’ [Thuis Upashaya is the eleventh Post, set up to the South of the other ten] In regard to thus Upashaya, there arises the question-Is it something consecrated-so that the culling and other consecratory acts are to be done to it, or not? < The Purvapaksa view is as follows “It should be consecrated, the cutting and other consecratory acts should be done to it,-why because the term connotes consecration; as a matter of fact, the term упра (Sacrificial Post) is used on the basis of consecration, and as such it cannot be applied to a post unless the consecratory acts have been performed, hence it follows that the consecratory acts should be performed (in con- nection with the Upashaya, which is the eleventh Sacrificial Post)” SUTRA (34) [SIDDHANTA-INASMUCH AS THE UPASHAYA DOES NOT FORM AN AUXILIARY TO THE SACRIFICE [IT NEED NOT BE CONSECRATED], [AS FOR THE NAME SACRIFICIAL POST’] THAT APPLIES TO IT FIGURATIVELY, BY REASON OF THE TERM CONNOTING CERTAIN QUALITIES (OF THE SACRIFICIAL POST) Bhasya. In reality, the consecratory acts are not to be performed in connection with the Upashaya —Why Because it does not form an auxiliary to the sacrifice The consecratory rites are performed in connection with the piece of wood (out of which the Post is made) with the view that through this wood-prece, they would become connected with the sacrificial act,-and the sacrifice performed with the animal tied to the Wood-piece thus conse- crated would accomplish the desired transcendental result -As regards the particular post, called Upashaya’, no animal is tied to it, so that if any consecratory rites were performed in connection with it, they would be 1296 SHABARA-BHASYA: futile-“On the strength of the declaration, those rites may be taken as serving some unseen purpose The answer to this is that, in tlus case, there is no such declaration as ’thus Sacrificial Post should be made’, all that the text does is to mention an existing fact The Upashaya is a Sacrificial Post As a matter of fact, in the absence of the consecratory rites, even the mention of the Upashaya being a Sacrificial Post as an existing fact, would not be right” -Our answer to this is that the name (‘Sacrificial Post’) would be applicable to the unconsecrated Upashaya figuratively, Just as in the case where the sacrificer is called ’the Sacrificial Post- ‘Yajamāno yūpah’-Says the Opponent’ In that case the name is applied figuratively by reason of similarity (between the Sacrificer and the Sacrificial Post); how would it apply to the Upashaya?”–The answer to this is that the term connotes certain qualities, ie the term ‘Sacrificial Post’ connotes certain qualities-embellishments of the Sacrificial Post, and some of these embellishments of the Sacrificial Post, such as cutting, scraping and the rest, are done, though silently (without Mantras) in the case of the Upashaya also, and it is on the basis of these that the name ‘Sacrificial Post’ is applied to it, though it is not really a Sacrificial Post’ Just as the maiden after bath, even though not decked in ornaments, is regarded as so decked even with a single string of the garland, so though only partly consecrated’ (embellished), the Upashaya is spoken of as consecrated (Sacrificial Post) by way of being eulogised. 4 C ADHIKARANA (14): In the sentence Prsthairupatisthante’, They worship with Prsthas’, the term ‘prstha’ stands for the words of the verses. Bhasya In connection with the Agrichayana, we read- Prsthairupatisthantë [‘They worship with Prathas ‘]. • In regard to this, there arises the question (A)-Are the details of the ‘Pratha’ to be applied to the Prsthas used at the Agnichayana ?—or not?
